affectedPublicSurfaces: THE AUTHENTICATED ACTION-CARD LIST — the first surface a seller actually sees change in this epic. A shop with clean orders due before the next window gains a PROCESS ORDER CARD; a shop with nothing due sees NO change at all. The card route itself is untouched: same path, same response model, same auth. What changes is that a card can now appear WITHOUT A SELLER TAP, because until this slice the only card producer is the manual `POST /v1/action-cards/refresh` (`api/routes/action_cards.py:89-130` → `services/action_cards/refresh.py`), and `workers/celery_app.py:40-91` carries six beat tasks, NONE of which produces a card or a run.

A NEW CELERY BEAT ENTRY — an operational surface and a standing commitment on a shared worker fleet. Its cadence (twice a day per shop), its behaviour on a MISSED TICK (the next run covers the gap, S-NFR-6, and does NOT emit a backlog of duplicate cards) and its per-shop fan-out are the release risk, not the code. It rides on #1711's scheduled-producer machinery rather than adding a second scheduling mechanism.

THE DISPATCH WINDOW AS A SUBJECT — ADR-092 d.1 amending ADR-087 d.5. A Juli entity of shop plus the deadline bucket one run covers, keyed so TWO RUNS CAN NEVER COVER THE SAME BUCKET. Today this is structurally impossible: `workflow_runs.product_id` is NOT NULL with the active-run index on `(shop, product)` (`models/models.py:576,620-627`) and `ActionCard` is unique on `(shop_id, workflow_key)` (`:953-957`) — one card per SHOP, not per subject. The window rides on #1702's card-resolved subject and #1701's nullable subject columns; this slice must not re-shape the active-run index beyond keying it on the window.

THE WINDOW CARD PAYLOAD — the count of clean orders, the EARLIEST DEADLINE, the orders split "due today" / "due tomorrow" and ordered by deadline INSIDE each bucket, and every excluded order with its reason. EVERY NUMBER IS COMPUTED BY THE PRODUCER (S-FR-4); the model picks none of them. #1801's payload and #1808's sheet both render from this shape, so a field named loosely here is a field two slices are stuck with.

SELLER-FACING COPY. All strings are Vietnamese through the seller-copy sanitiser (`services/agent/sanitize`), and no order id, window id or exclusion enum may reach the seller (S-NFR-4). This is the first Process Order copy anyone reads.

TENANCY (ADR-089, S-NFR-8). Every tenant read in the beat task runs under `with_shop_scope`; the shop enumeration is the one sanctioned unscoped step. A fleet-wide read 'just to find the due orders' is the precise anti-pattern.

SUPPRESSION IS A FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME. A shop with nothing due emits NO card and records a NAMED SUPPRESSION REASON — 'nothing to do' is never a failure (S-FR-7), and an absent card with no reason is indistinguishable from a producer that crashed.
NO new HTTP route and NO change to any response model.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest from the WORKTREE ROOT with PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree's own `backend/src`, against a REAL Postgres 16 migrated to head — never SQLite. The window key's uniqueness, the active-run index, RLS, the `juli_app` role's per-table grants and the GUC-backed tenant context are all Postgres behaviour with no SQLite equivalent, and a cross-tenant assertion run without RLS or run as the table owner proves nothing. The producer is exercised as the REAL beat task with the REAL `with_shop_scope` and the REAL predicate from #1797 — not a stub verdict — and cards are emitted through #1703's subject-scoped emission path rather than by inserting an `action_cards` row by hand. Post-deploy: run the producer ONCE on the candidate against the SANDBOX shop, read the card back through the AUTHENTICATED card route, and confirm `/health` and one authenticated read are unchanged for a shop with nothing due; no public traffic reaches the candidate and NO vendor write occurs.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: workersDisabledOnCandidate is FALSE because the entire slice IS a beat task; a candidate with workers disabled can never produce a window card, which is the whole slice. apiSideEffectsInScope is FALSE: the only rows written are each shop's own `action_cards` and the window subject row, through #1703's emission path; the producer reads orders and makes NO vendor write. NO PACKAGE IS SHIPPED ON ANY SHOP BY DEPLOYING THIS SLICE — a card is a proposal a human has not yet approved, there is no ship tool registered yet (#1803), and an unconfirmed window simply expires. The first live proof of the write is the #1806 dry run, then the seeded sandbox batch (#1810), never production, which stays gated on #1339 (S-NFR-3).

journeys.name: one-window-one-card-computed-by-the-producer-under-each-shops-own-tenant-scope
assertions: pre-merge: with a shop whose clean orders are due before the next scheduled run, the producer creates EXACTLY ONE card for that window BOUND TO THE WINDOW AS ITS SUBJECT, and a SECOND producer pass over the same window creates NO second card — asserted on the `action_cards` rows and the subject binding, not on a call count (tests/unit/test_dispatch_window_producer.py::test_one_card_per_window_and_no_duplicate)

pre-merge: a shop with no order due before the next run emits NO card and the SUPPRESSION CARRIES A NAMED REASON — a positive recorded fact, never the mere absence of a card, because 'nothing due' and 'the producer raised' must not look alike (tests/unit/test_dispatch_window_producer.py::test_nothing_due_suppresses_with_a_named_reason)

pre-merge: with clean orders across two buckets and two excluded orders, the card payload carries the COUNT, the EARLIEST DEADLINE, BOTH buckets ordered by deadline, and EACH exclusion with its reason; moving one order's deadline past midnight MOVES IT BETWEEN BUCKETS — the bucket boundary is derived from the deadline, not hard-coded (tests/unit/test_dispatch_window_card_payload.py::test_payload_carries_count_earliest_deadline_buckets_and_exclusions)

pre-merge: with two tenants each holding due orders, the beat task produces each shop's card UNDER ITS OWN TENANT SCOPE and NO query reads across tenants — asserted on the tenant context actually in force during each producer call and AS THE RUNTIME ROLE `juli_app` UNDER RLS, so a read that escaped `with_shop_scope` returns zero rows and raises the named application error (ADR-086) rather than quietly succeeding (tests/unit/test_dispatch_window_producer.py::test_producer_runs_under_per_tenant_scope)

pre-merge: no seller-facing string in the built payload contains an ORDER ID, a WINDOW ID or an EXCLUSION ENUM, and all of them are Vietnamese — asserted through the real outbound guard at `services/agent/sanitize`, not by a regex written in the test (tests/unit/test_dispatch_window_card_payload.py::test_seller_copy_carries_no_internal_identifier)

pre-merge: a MISSED cadence is tolerated — skipping a tick does not emit a backlog of duplicate cards, because #1703's `active_card_exists`/`basis_unchanged` suppression engages (S-NFR-6); asserted by counting rows after a skipped tick

htmlRoutes: No HTML route, page, bundle or static asset changes. The diff is `workers/tasks/process_order_windows.py`, `workers/celery_app.py`, `services/agent/workflows/process_order/window.py`, `models/models.py`, one additive Alembic migration and tests. The demo surfaces that render this payload are #1808; nothing under apps/, packages/ or ios/ is touched here, and those are on this epic's doNotLoad list.

migrationCompatibility.notes: ONE ADDITIVE, EXPAND-ONLY migration: the dispatch-window subject row and the NULLABLE window reference on the run and the card, laid over #1702/#1701's NULLABLE subject columns and their `subject_type`/`subject_ref` vocabulary rather than inventing a second one, plus the per-shop window/cadence rows the producer schedules from. No column is dropped, renamed or retyped; `product_id` stays as #1701 left it; there is no backfill and no NOT NULL, and an ABSENT cadence row means NOT ENROLLED — it must never default to a firing time, because a defaulted midnight would silently enrol every existing shop in a scheduled producer they never asked for. Store the local times WITH their IANA zone: `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` is UTC+7, and a naive column makes a shop configured for 06:00 local fire at 06:00 UTC. THE MIGRATION NUMBER AND `down_revision` ARE RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename — this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files from exactly that mistake, and W6, W7-bis, W9 and W10-A all hold unlanded numbers off-tree. `workflow_runs` and `action_cards` are tenant-scoped and already carry RLS policies from `045_rls_policies.py`, so no new policy is created — but the new columns must be covered by the runtime role's existing per-table grants from `043_juli_app_role.py` (ADR-085), asserted as `juli_app` and never as the owner. Old and new code coexist: the previous release neither reads nor writes the window columns and has no beat entry to fire.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing schedules anything: approval stays the only `WorkflowRun(` site, card refresh stays manual, and the dispatch window has no substrate — which is the pre-existing state, so no seller sees anything different. A half-landed producer is worse than none: a beat entry that emits cards for a window nobody can confirm would put an unactionable Process Order card in front of every enrolled shop.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: REMOVE THE BEAT ENTRY FIRST — with no producer there is no new card, and that alone stops the bleeding without touching the schema. Then redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker: the previous code neither reads nor writes the window columns, so it runs correctly with them present and needs NO downgrade; window rows and window-subject cards are INERT to it, though a card written since cutover will remain in the seller's list until it is expired or suppressed — expire them explicitly rather than leaving a card whose workflow no longer exists. Only if the schema must also be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1` drops the window columns and rows; it MUST FAIL LOUDLY, never silently, when any run is still bound to a window subject, because dropping the subject out from under a live run strands it until its reaper timer fires. Order: beat entry off, previous code, downgrade last. Nothing in either direction may ship a package: there is no write path in this slice.

acceptanceCommands: PYTHONPATH=backend/src python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'action_card or tenant_scope or rls or subject'
ruff check backend tests scripts && ruff format --check backend tests scripts
doNotInfer: The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. This slice DOES carry a migration, so the reservation is binding.

Do NOT auto-ship on expiry, and do NOT add a standing or repeat approval. An unconfirmed window simply expires and the next scheduled run re-proposes with urgency marked (ADR-092 d.3). The standing approval is the DEFERRED option 2 and needs the autonomy ladder.

Do NOT let the model choose the count, the earliest deadline, the bucket membership or the ordering. The producer computes every number (S-FR-4); the model picks subject, wording and whether to proceed.

Do NOT re-shape the active-run index beyond keying it on the window, and do NOT change the subject vocabulary #1701/#1702 established. A second `subject_type` spelling is a second answer to a solved question.

Do NOT build a second scheduling mechanism. The producer rides on #1711's scheduled-producer machinery and #1703's subject-scoped emission path; a bespoke beat loop or a hand-inserted `action_cards` row bypasses the suppression and revision semantics that make a missed tick safe.

Do NOT do a fleet-wide read. Shop enumeration is the one sanctioned unscoped step; every tenant read after it runs inside `with_shop_scope` (ADR-089, S-NFR-8), and tenancy is asserted as `juli_app` under RLS, never as the table owner.
Do NOT store a local firing time without its IANA zone, and do NOT default an absent cadence row to a firing time. Absent means NOT ENROLLED.
Do NOT define the confirmation payload, do NOT re-verify, do NOT execute, and do NOT register a ship tool. Those are #1801 and #1803.

Do NOT build a vendor-refusal branch anywhere in the producer or the predicate call. TikTok does NOT refuse a ship write during a pending cancellation (ADR-092 amendment 2026-09-05) — the exclusion is hard, in Juli's own code.

Do NOT recompute a cutoff when the order carries a deadline field. Use #1797's ladder — `rts_sla_time` → `tts_sla_time` → `collection_due_time` — with the rung recorded; the documented cutoff is the last resort only.
Do NOT propose, request or write a cancellation for any excluded order. No cancel tool exists in this allowlist, ever.

Do NOT add a Create Packages or a Confirm Package Shipment step: in SEA TikTok creates the package at order time, and Confirm Package Shipment is certified-warehouse-provider-only (ADR-092 Context defects 1 and 2).
Do NOT act on FBT or Seller Own Fleet orders. v1 is fulfilled-by-seller with platform shipping only; both are LISTED with their reasons and never acted on.
Do NOT let an order id, a window id or an exclusion enum reach a seller-facing string, and do NOT write English copy. Everything goes through the outbound guard at `services/agent/sanitize`.
Do NOT verify with a success-marker grep. A beat task that raises before it logs is invisible to one; assert on the card row, the suppression record and the running app's own beat schedule.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/**, which are on this epic's doNotLoad list.
